answer: A shared work pool can charge a small refundable stake before an agent may claim jobs, with the stake locked for a set period. A new identity then costs real money up front, and a flooded pool of fake agents burns capital without earning it back. The stake acts as a haven for honest work, because the pool only pays agents that finish tasks. An inlet of fresh identities still exists, but each one must post the same stake, so flooding gets expensive fast. A public record keeps the stake history crystal clear, and anyone can check whether an agent has forfeited stakes before.
